rationale: No abstract; a short JSAP item on autochthonous babesiosis that may describe presentation and treatment. Cannot tell whether treatment or outcome is reported.
Title indicates a letter on drug availability, with no treated dogs or presentation described.
Fluralaner tick-transmission prevention trial in uninfected dogs; endpoint is infection prevented, with no clinical disease treated.
One dog with fever, anaemia, thrombocytopenia and splenomegaly treated with a 10-day drug combination; improved from day 4 and recovered.

The abstract field holds only the title and affiliation. The title suggests cryopreserved red cell transfusion for anaemia in canine babesiosis, and the earlier rationale mentions Hb/Hct rises against untransfused dogs, but the abstract itself is missing.
Russian-language duplicate of the cryopreserved red cell paper with a citation line only. The title suggests treatment of anaemic syndrome in B. canis dogs, but no abstract is available.
No abstract. The title describes clinical management of one dog co-infected with Leptospira, B. gibsoni and Dirofilaria; it is unclear whether babesiosis treatment and outcome are reported.
Review of the diagnostic protocol that also covers therapy management and drug response by Babesia species. Treatment is part of the subject, though the emphasis is on diagnosis.
Nursing overview of several tick-borne diseases. The abstract mentions limits in diagnosis and treatment but does not show that babesiosis treatment is covered.

No abstract. The title and earlier note describe experimental B. vogeli infection treated with imidocarb and/or alpha-lipoic acid, with clinical and haematological endpoints, so it is probably an include.
No abstract. The title suggests plasmapheresis for polyorgan intoxication in Babesia-infected dogs, but design and outcomes are unknown.
No abstract. The title indicates therapeutic management of hepatic failure and ascites in one B. gibsoni dog, which probably qualifies, but no content is available.

Secondary IMHA dogs, 13 of them with B. gibsoni, treated with prednisolone with or without azathioprine plus specific therapy. Hb, PCV, platelets and clinical improvement to day 28 are reported, but the Babesia subgroup is mixed with other causes.
One dog with AKI after treated babesiosis, managed with haemodialysis and recovering renal function. The Babesia link is asserted but not documented in detail.
Comparison of homeopathic Crotalus horridus (13 dogs) with diminazene (20 dogs) in B. gibsoni dogs with listed clinical signs. Clinical scores and parasitaemia improved in both groups.
No abstract. The title describes peritoneal dialysis for acute renal failure in a B. canis dog, which is likely an include, but outcome is not confirmed.

One dog with icterus, weakness and suspected cerebral babesiosis that did not respond to treatment and was found post mortem to have rabies. Treatment drugs are not named in the abstract, so this is borderline.

Naturally infected dogs treated with atovaquone plus azithromycin (17) or clindamycin, diminazene and imidocarb (13). Recovery, relapse and therapy duration are reported, and haematology was recorded.
No abstract. The title describes cutaneous lesions in one dog with babesiosis, but treatment and outcome cannot be confirmed.
